newsitem.title: USA: Christian Coalition head defends Gingrich.
newsitem.headline: Christian Coalition head defends Gingrich.

text.p: Ralph Reed, director of the influential Christian Coalition, offered a spirited defence Monday of embattled Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich.

Gingrich has been under fire recently from conservatives in his own party. Some have even urged him to resign the speakership, saying he has lost his revolutionary zeal and is compromising too much with President Clinton and Democrats.
"Newt Gingrich remains not only an asset but an indispensible asset to the Republican Party and the conservative cause and I am proud to call him my friend," Reed said.

Reed's endorsement, offered in a speech to GOPAC, a political action committee founded by Gingrich, may take some pressure off the Speaker, who was fined $300,000 by the House for ethical violations last January and is currently weighing whether to pay out of his own pocket or from campaign funds.
Reed praised Gingrich's recent trip to Asia, saying he had represented the United States far better in China than Vice President Al Gore did during an earlier visit.
